svg.title: M14: A measured breach becomes a verified governance handoff
svg.desc: An accepted Control 9 crossing creates a durable alert intent. The permitted ServiceNow route is asynchronous. A lost response remains uncertain until conclusive reconciliation; correct-instance content and recipient readback establish dated platform delivery. Performance breach, alert delivery, response observation and remediation are separate states. Evidence flows back to M06 and M13.

g.text: M14 / GOVERNANCE AND HUMAN OVERSIGHT / PROPOSED DESIGN
A delivered alert does not turn a breach into a pass.
Illustrative Control 9 story • no live ServiceNow write or human response claimed

g.title: Accepted Control 9 assessment with pinned evidence and rule
g.text: 1. M08 assessment
12% drop > 10% limit
Control + rule + window
Accepted revision + sources

g.title: Durable required alert intent with stable finding identity
g.text: 2. M14 intent / outbox
Stable finding identity
Revisioned delivery operation
Verified route + named owner
Independent of LLM availability

g.title: Actual permitted target, asynchronous dispatch, bounded attempts
g.text: 3. ServiceNow route
Authorized instance / workflow
Actual permitted operations
Asynchronous worker
No inference wait for delivery

g.title: The assessment creates an intent, which a worker dispatches to the permitted route
Reconcile the actual remote outcome using verified receiver semantics and content readback
g.text: 4. Reconcile and read back the actual remote outcome
Check instance, correlation, intended revision/content and named-recipient route.
A local key, HTTP acknowledgement or remote ID alone does not prove the intended delivery.

g.title: Unresolved possible writes and verified delivery are different outcomes
Unknown outcome remains unresolved without a safe receiver-supported recovery
g.text: OUTCOME UNKNOWN
Possible write: retain uncertainty; no blind create retry.
Empty eventual lookup ≠ proof of absence.
Resolve through verified semantics or an operator.

g.title: Readback proves dated platform delivery, not human engagement
g.text: DELIVERED · AS OF READBACK
Intended record and named recipient verified.
Notification dispatch and human reply are separate.
Human reply is not required by the hackathon.

g.title: The example records separate requirement, delivery, response and remediation states
Illustrative outcome after a verified handoff with covered silence
g.text: The judge sees four independent facts
Performance: BREACHED · Alert: DELIVERED · Response: not observed · Remediation: OPEN
Silence has a stated cutoff and response-source coverage. Missing visibility means RESPONSE UNKNOWN.

g.title: Delivery and response observations return as source evidence for query and export
g.text: Delivery / response / retest records → M05 + M06 evidence → M13 case → M15 export
Remediation needs a relevant passing retest. Authoritative correction is a different disposition.
